The load address is `y0 + 128*x2 + 4032000*y1` — consecutive threads in the x-warp step by 128 elements in the input (stride-128 access), causing every load to miss L1 (0% hit rate) and saturate L2 at 97%. The current XBLOCK=128, YBLOCK=8 tile means 128 threads each load from addresses 128 apart, which is maximally non-coalesced. Increasing YBLOCK (so more y-rows are processed per CTA) and reducing XBLOCK improves the ratio of coalesced y-dimension accesses (stride-1 in y0) relative to the strided x-dimension accesses. Adding @triton.autotune lets the runtime find the best tile shape that maximizes L1 reuse and coalescing for this specific transpose pattern.
